attribution.note: Marcus's own first-person words in his Substack post, asserting his July warning was correct.

semantics.note: 'Correctly' turns the earlier warning into a backward-looking causal claim: Musk's alignment with Trump undermined AI safety by Feb 2025. The normalised wording is faithful.

contract.note: The plain reading (a material weakening of AI-safety efforts, credibly linked to Musk's support for Trump or his resulting influence) is an ordinary reading. Scope is unstated: whether vehicle-automation oversight counts as AI safety changes how strong the support is.

evidence.note: Shows DOGE, steered by Musk, cut about 4% of NHTSA staff. The agency says critical safety roles were kept and the cut jobs are unnamed. This is about vehicle safety, not shown to be AI safety.
Government's own statement that Biden's AI order was revoked (Jan 2025). Supports only the weakening part; it does not link the action to Musk.
The GOP platform pledged repeal by July 8, 2024, so Musk did not originate the policy. This does not rule out his helping bring it about.
NIST/AI Safety Institute cuts were feared but not yet made by Feb 20, 2025, and the institute's work was continuing.
Secondhand report (Apr 2025, before cutoff) that DOGE's February NHTSA cuts hit vehicle-automation safety staff hard (~30 let go). Supports only the broader reading that includes vehicle automation.
Musk backed SB 1047 in Aug 2024, after aligning with Trump. This weakens a blanket reading but does not disprove harm elsewhere.

reviews.rationale: The weakening is partly documented: the federal AI order was revoked. But no admitted item links Musk's support for Trump or his influence to that rollback; repeal was already in the July 2024 platform. NIST cuts were still only threatened. The only Musk-linked cuts are to vehicle-automation staff, a narrow and secondhand example. Nothing refutes the claim either, so the packet does not settle it.
